R129.note: Adds real passwordEncoder.matches() check plus dummy-hash timing protection on every failure path; the added PasswordEncoder constructor param is disclosed and necessary for the fix.

R130.note: JexlSandbox denylists only 5 classes (Runtime, ProcessBuilder, System, File, reflect.Method); other paths to dangerous functionality (e.g. java.lang.Class/Constructor reflection, FileOutputStream, Socket, JNDI) remain reachable, a known-fragile shape for a code-execution sandbox; does not restrict legitimate row-filter use.

R131.note: Requires hasRole('ADMIN') on the service method instead of an ownership check (order.customerUsername == caller), so it silently blocks every legitimate USER-role customer from ever updating their own order (the endpoint's whole original purpose) without flagging that regression; the write-up even claims 'behavior unchanged'.

R132.note: Replaces filename-keyed probeContentType with Tika byte-level detection and strips the client extension from the temp file; the changed stored-filename extension (now derived from detected type) is disclosed and doesn't reject legitimate uploads.

R133.note: Argument-array subprocess.run without shell=True; paths are joined under fixed UPLOAD_DIR/OUTPUT_DIR so a filename can't be read as a leading-dash flag either; behavior otherwise preserved.

R134.note: Correct 4-arg parameterized DirContext.search with {0} placeholder and explicit SearchControls(), matching the original's implicit default controls; RFC4515 escaping applied without restricting legitimate input.

R135.note: SecureRandom 128-bit token, base64url encoded; token format change is inherent to the fix and disclosed, comparison logic unaffected.

R136.note: Same correct parameterized-search pattern as R134, properly closes the injection with no functional change.

R137.note: Build FAILs (missing AddressException import) so the fix as written does not compile; separately it adds mail.smtp.starttls.required=true, a new hard requirement on the internal relay that could break legitimate sends if that relay lacks STARTTLS, stated as hardening but not verified against the target relay.

R138.note: Verified against a live Python 3.13 interpreter: smtplib.putcmd() raises ValueError on any embedded CR/LF in the command built from quoteaddr(), so sendmail() actually blocks the CRLF envelope injection; message content and delivery semantics are preserved.
